373a59b7-e7b2-80ad-a237-c35bd18d572b.notes:
• Notification Workflow: Fixed primary contact email alerts by updating workflow variables; manual emails used temporarily to ensure delivery.
• Timesheet Reporting: Editing limited to list view; custom dashboards for billable/admin time in development with planned calendar/Gantt views.
• Customer Data Import: Vendor/third-party customer types added with two years of ticket history; inactive users imported and manageable.
• Mobile App Features: Supports task scheduling, travel/work timers, basic parts search; lacks timesheet summaries and ticket printing.
• Payment Integration: TRX and ACH processors setup underway; legal review pending for credit card convenience fees in Connecticut.
• Data Migration: Tiger Paw data import planned for next Monday with post-migration review; community requests to address workflow fixes.Notes
Workflow and Notification Setup
The team resolved key issues with ticket notification workflows to ensure correct email alerts reach primary and secondary contacts.
• Primary contact email notifications fixed by adjusting workflow variables (13:21)
    ◦ Clarified that ticket primary contact differs from customer primary contact, requiring different workflow variables.
    ◦ Mark identified correct checkboxes to notify all designated contacts without manually entering emails.
    ◦ Steve realized the need to update the ticket’s primary contact field, not just the customer’s, for notifications to work.
    ◦ This update will ensure notifications reach the correct stakeholders automatically.
• Workflows for multiple email notifications consolidated and tested (02:54)
    ◦ Steve initially combined multiple email actions in one workflow due to failure when split into two workflows.
    ◦ Mark suggested separate workflows for different email content but acknowledged current limitations.
    ◦ The workflow sends notifications correctly to internal users and ticket submitters but needed refinement for external contacts.
• Timezone discrepancy in scheduled work notifications identified (06:46)
    ◦ Steve reported scheduled work emails showing times in GMT, causing a 4-hour offset for East Coast users.
    ◦ Mark confirmed the issue relates to the start date variable sending GMT times.
    ◦ This will be addressed to ensure customer communications reflect correct local times and avoid confusion.
• Manual email entries used as temporary workaround for missing notifications (24:59)
    ◦ To guarantee notification delivery, Mark manually added email addresses in workflows alongside automatic contact variables.
    ◦ This ensures key people receive emails regardless of variable limitations during the transition period.
Timesheet and Reporting Enhancements
The team discussed improvements to timesheet editing and reporting to streamline time tracking and payroll processes.
• Timesheet editing limited to list view, not calendar view, prompting feature request (39:42)
    ◦ Steve noted inability to edit time entries directly from the calendar-style timesheet view despite full permissions.
    ◦ Mark confirmed this is a current system limitation and plans to request the feature from the product team.
    ◦ Improving this will reduce extra steps and help quickly correct time entries.
• Development of custom dashboards for billable and admin time reporting underway (46:05)
    ◦ Mark demonstrated a time details dashboard showing individual tech time entries with filters by week and task type.
    ◦ The dashboard currently totals billable hours but can be expanded to include admin hours as Steve requested.
    ◦ Scheduled weekly reports can be automatically emailed to managers summarizing each tech’s time for payroll accuracy.
• Plan to create calendar and Gantt chart views to complement list reports (49:29)
    ◦ Mark suggested adding calendar or Gantt chart visualizations to better track daily time distribution.
    ◦ Steve agreed that separate views for admin (clock in/out) and billable time would be useful.
    ◦ These enhancements aim to provide clearer, more actionable views of technician time usage.
• Community requests planned for additional timesheet and reporting features (41:13)
    ◦ Steve will submit requests for mobile app timesheet views showing gaps or missing entries for easier technician self-auditing.
    ◦ The team also plans to request audit logging of sent emails to verify workflow notifications.
Customer and Contact Data Management
The team aligned on handling customer types and data import to support multi-contact and vendor distinctions.
• Customer type field to support vendors and third parties upon data import (33:32)
    ◦ Jessica clarified the need to differentiate vendors, third-party customers, and regular customers using the type field.
    ◦ Mark confirmed types will be added during import from Tiger Paw, allowing filtering and segmentation.
    ◦ Users can add or inactivate types but not delete them, supporting flexibility in categorization.
• Inactive users and two years of ticket history will be imported by next week (18:43)
    ◦ Mark confirmed the entire user base, including inactive staff, will migrate to maintain ticket integrity.
    ◦ Ticket history will span the last two years to preserve essential service records.
    ◦ Inactive users can be hidden via filters, keeping active user lists clean.
• Plans to add customer balance due field to customer list for quick payment visibility (09:42)
    ◦ Steve requested adding balance due to the customer list view to easily spot customers with outstanding payments.
    ◦ This will be submitted to the community forum for prioritization.
    ◦ It will improve collections and customer account management efficiency.
Mobile App Usage and Features
The team reviewed mobile app capabilities for technicians to manage schedules, tickets, and time tracking remotely.
• Mobile app supports calendar, ticket, customer views, and task scheduling (23:48)
    ◦ Mark demonstrated scheduling tasks on the mobile calendar and linking them to tickets for technician visibility.
    ◦ Tapping addresses opens maps apps for navigation; Google Maps integration works smoothly.
    ◦ The app allows viewing ticket details and customer info, aiding field service management.
• Travel and work timers mimic desktop app functionality with geofencing (27:17)
    ◦ Travel timers start and stop based on location boundaries, automatically logging travel time.
    ◦ Travel time defaults to billable but can be adjusted; permissions to restrict changes are limited.
    ◦ Work timers start after travel ends, enabling accurate job time tracking.
• Parts search in mobile app is name-based, no ID or serial number search yet (33:59)
    ◦ Steve confirmed product search only matches product names, not ID numbers, simplifying lookup.
    ◦ Barcode scanning requires pre-existing serial numbers in the system and is not broadly useful currently.
    ◦ This aligns with current non-serialized product tracking practices.
• Mobile app lacks timesheet summary and print ticket features, planned community requests (39:32, 45:44)
    ◦ Steve emphasized need for a mobile timesheet view to track daily time completion and spot gaps.
    ◦ Printing or emailing completed ticket PDFs is not yet available on mobile; desktop app supports PDF generation.
    ◦ The team plans to request enhancements to automate ticket PDF emailing upon completion.
Payment Processing and Integration
The team reviewed payment integration setup, fees, and legal considerations for credit card surcharges.
• Payment processors setup underway with TRX and ACH integration planned (12:39, 56:37)
    ◦ Mark to configure payment processors in the system for credit card and ACH payments using existing TRX login.
    ◦ Jessica and Steve to verify TRX account status and legal limits for surcharges in Connecticut.
    ◦ Mark will coordinate with payment experts to finalize integration.
• Credit card convenience fees configurable but legal options unclear (15:39)
    ◦ System allows adding percentage fees (e.g., 1.5% or 3%) labeled as credit card or convenience fees.
    ◦ Steve noted Connecticut law may prohibit surcharges labeled as credit card fees, requiring legal review.
    ◦ Jessica to investigate and clarify compliance before fees are applied.
• ACH payment fees acknowledged but currently borne by customers via banks (17:04)
    ◦ The team recognized fees exist for ACH but are not charged directly in the system currently.
    ◦ Setup will maintain this approach unless changes are required.
Data Migration and Next Steps
The team set expectations for the upcoming data migration and follow-up activities.
• Database migration to Tiger Paw replacement planned for early next week (18:00)
    ◦ Mark confirmed the customer and ticket data import will complete by next Monday.
    ◦ Migration includes all active and inactive users, two years of ticket history, and product data without inventory management.
• Post-migration review and error correction scheduled (57:30)
    ◦ Mark will notify the team when the data is live for validation.
    ◦ Any migration errors or inconsistencies are expected and will be fixed promptly.
• Community requests for missing features and workflow fixes to be submitted immediately (55:51)
    ◦ Key issues include correcting time zone displays, external party email notifications, and editable timesheet views.
    ◦ Steve encouraged submitting requests early to prioritize development alongside new features like ticket printing.
• Next formal meeting scheduled for June 26th with Griff to demonstrate analytics and workflows (07:43)
    ◦ The team will review progress and new features after data migration.
    ◦ Mark to complete payment processor setup and coordinate with reporting experts before then.Action itemsMark Kephart
